s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of painless nodules with ulceration and hemorrhagic crusts on the fingers, accompanied by discomfort and pain along the arm and forearm
salient_findings: Vesicles that ruptured and formed hemorrhagic crusts
Discomfort and pain along the medial aspect of the arm and forearm
Similar lesions on the cow's teats
key_facts: 30-year-old male
Dairy farm worker
Multiple painless nodules on fingers of both hands
Nodules appeared 1 month prior to presentation
Vesicles developed 7-10 days after initial nodules
Hemorrhagic crusts formed after vesicle rupture
Discomfort and pain along the medial aspect of the right arm and forearm
Denies trauma or insect bites
Cow had similar lesions on its teats
3-4 firm, non-tender nodules with central hemorrhagic crusts and surrounding erythema on the proximal phalanges of both hands
Mild tenderness and increased warmth along the medial right arm and forearm

shortlist.label: Orf virus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Occupational exposure to livestock and characteristic skin lesions

shortlist.label: Milker's nodule
shortlist.why_kept: Painless nodules with ulceration and hemorrhagic crusts in a dairy farm worker

shortlist.label: Pseudocowpox
shortlist.why_kept: Similar lesions on the cow's teats and patient's hands

shortlist.label: Erysipeloid
shortlist.why_kept: Occupational exposure to livestock and skin lesions with central ulceration

shortlist.label: Paravaccinia virus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Similar skin lesions and occupational exposure to livestock

shortlist.label: Bovine papular stomatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar skin lesions and occupational exposure to livestock

shortlist.label: Cowpox
shortlist.why_kept: Similar skin lesions and potential exposure to infected animals

shortlist.label: Vesicular stomatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar skin lesions and potential exposure to infected animals

raw.rationale: The patient's occupation as a dairy farm worker, the presence of similar lesions on the cow's teats, and the characteristic skin lesions with central hemorrhagic crusts and surrounding erythema are consistent with Milker's nodule, also known as paravaccinia or pseudocowpox, but given the options, Milker's nodule is the most fitting diagnosis.

rejected.label: Orf virus infection
rejected.why: While Orf virus infection can cause similar lesions, it is more commonly associated with direct contact with infected sheep or goats, rather than cows.

rejected.label: Pseudocowpox
rejected.why: Pseudocowpox is another term for Milker's nodule, so it is not a distinct diagnosis to reject.

rejected.label: Erysipeloid
rejected.why: Erysipeloid typically presents with a well-demarcated, erythematous lesion, often with a distinctive 'coin-like' shape, which does not match the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Paravaccinia virus infection
rejected.why: Paravaccinia virus infection is another term for Milker's nodule, so it is not a distinct diagnosis to reject.

rejected.label: Bovine papular stomatitis
rejected.why: Bovine papular stomatitis primarily affects the oral mucosa of cattle and is not typically associated with skin lesions in humans.

rejected.label: Cowpox
rejected.why: Cowpox is a more severe disease that can affect a wider range of animals and humans, often with more systemic symptoms, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Vesicular stomatitis
rejected.why: Vesicular stomatitis is a viral disease that primarily affects livestock, causing vesicular lesions on the oral mucosa, and is not typically associated with the skin lesions described in this patient.
